newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest shares close mixed, outlook firm.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest shares close mixed, outlook firm.

text.p: Bucharest bourse shares traded sideways on Tuesday amid thin buying interest which led to lacklustre trading, brokers said.
But they said that some high-caps might gain steam on Wednesday, with big players expected to put some pressure on bid sides.
"Heavy-weights might recoup part of their recent losses," one trader said. "We expect buyers to return to the market. There are no reasons for further falls in high-caps."

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, inched up from the previous session, gaining 1.2, 1.35 and 1.19 percent, respectively.
The closing prices of 18 stocks grew, 18 went down and eight stocks were unchanged. Two companies were suspended and another two had no trades.
On the first-tier, four listings closed weaker in late trading, after touching higher prices at mid-day.

Azomures fertiliser maker lost 200 lei to close 3,800 in active trading. Chemical plant Oltchim shed 50 lei to close at 4,400. Both pharmaceutical plants Terapia and Antibiotice stayed flat on the previous session, at 8,150 and, respectively, 11,600 lei.
Traders expected some selling pressure on Terapia and Antibiotice on Wednesday, saying their prices were still too high.
Second tier activity remained slack despite rising interest in small-caps as liquidity of the section's 40 listings was relatively low, brokers said.
One trader said investors might extend their buying pressure to lure second-tier stocks' owners to sell.
